new_task_1.title: Allow partial fill_value mappings in Dataset.unstack()
new_task_1.description: Dataset.unstack() now accepts a fill_value mapping that specifies replacements for only some variables. Previously, if fill_value was a Mapping and a variable name was absent from that mapping, unstack would index the mapping directly and raise a KeyError. The new behavior uses Mapping.get(name, NA), so unspecified variables fall back to xarray's default missing-value sentinel instead of failing.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset.unstack() works when fill_value is provided as a mapping that only covers a subset of variables. Previously, users had to supply fill values for every unstacked variable or risk a KeyError when an omitted variable was encountered.

expectation.grounded: In Dataset.unstack(), when iterating over variables to apply fill values, a mapping-valued fill_value must be resolved with fill_value.get(name, xrdtypes.NA) instead of direct indexing. This means variables present in the mapping use their explicit replacement value, while variables not present fall back to xarray's default NA behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to override fill values only for the variables they care about when unstacking a Dataset. Any other variables should continue to receive the normal missing-value fill behavior rather than causing the operation to fail.

constraints.grounded: Non-mapping fill_value inputs must continue to apply the same scalar fill value to all relevant variables. Mapping entries that are present must still take precedence for their corresponding variable names. Unspecified variables must default to xrdtypes.NA rather than inheriting another variable's fill value or raising an exception.
constraints.conceptual: This fix must be backward compatible for existing scalar fill_value usage and for complete mappings. The only behavioral change should be that partial mappings become valid and use the standard default fill semantics for omitted variables.

behavior: Dataset.unstack(fill_value={...}) no longer requires the mapping to include every variable name in the Dataset.
When a variable name is present in the fill_value mapping, Dataset.unstack() uses the mapped fill value for that variable.
When a variable name is absent from the fill_value mapping, Dataset.unstack() uses xarray's default missing-value sentinel (xrdtypes.NA) for that variable.
The operation no longer raises KeyError solely because a fill_value mapping omits some variables.
acceptance_criteria: When Dataset.unstack() is called with a scalar fill_value, behavior remains unchanged from prior versions.
When Dataset.unstack() is called with a mapping that contains entries for all variables, behavior remains unchanged from prior versions.
When Dataset.unstack() is called with a mapping that specifies only one variable, the named variable uses the provided fill value and other variables are filled with the default NA behavior.
When a Dataset contains multiple variables and one is omitted from the fill_value mapping, Dataset.unstack() completes successfully without raising KeyError.

new_task_2.title: Preserve custom colormap extremes in discrete plotting
new_task_2.description: Discrete plotting now preserves user-customized colormap extreme colors more reliably when building a discrete colormap. In _build_discrete_cmap(), xarray now detects real Matplotlib Colormap objects, reads the bad/under/over colors from the source colormap, suppresses under/over only when they are still the default endpoint colors, and applies the result with with_extremes(). This avoids losing explicitly configured bad/under/over colors when plotting with discrete levels.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray's discrete plotting helpers preserve explicitly customized bad, under, and over colors from a Matplotlib colormap. Previously, these colors could be lost or copied inconsistently when xarray rebuilt a discrete colormap for contour-style plots.

expectation.grounded: In xarray.plot.utils._build_discrete_cmap(), when cmap is an instance of mpl.colors.Colormap, xarray must read bad via cmap(np.nan), inspect under via cmap(-np.inf) and over via cmap(np.inf), treat under/over as unset when they match the colormap's default low/high endpoint colors, and then create the discrete colormap with new_cmap.with_extremes(bad=bad, under=under, over=over).
expectation.conceptual: If a user customizes a colormap's extreme colors and then uses an xarray plotting method that discretizes that colormap, the rendered plot should keep those custom extreme colors instead of silently reverting to defaults.

constraints.grounded: The special handling must only run for actual Matplotlib Colormap instances. Inputs such as colormap names or color lists must continue to bypass extreme-color copying. Under and over colors should only be carried over when the source colormap has explicitly changed them from its default endpoint colors.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must preserve user customization without forcing non-default extreme colors onto colormaps that were never customized. Existing behavior for non-Colormap cmap inputs must remain unchanged.

behavior: When a Matplotlib Colormap with a custom bad color is used for discrete plotting, the resulting discrete colormap preserves that bad color.
When a Matplotlib Colormap with a custom under color is used for discrete plotting, the resulting discrete colormap preserves that under color.
When a Matplotlib Colormap with a custom over color is used for discrete plotting, the resulting discrete colormap preserves that over color.
When the source colormap's under or over colors are still the default endpoint colors, xarray leaves them unset on the discrete colormap rather than forcing redundant values.
String-based or list-based cmap inputs continue to skip extreme-color copying logic.
acceptance_criteria: When plotting with a Matplotlib Colormap whose bad, under, and over colors have all been explicitly customized, the discrete colormap used by xarray preserves those custom colors.
When plotting with a Matplotlib Colormap whose under and over colors remain at their defaults, xarray preserves the bad color but does not force custom under/over values onto the discrete colormap.
When cmap is provided as a string name or a list of colors, xarray continues to build a discrete colormap without attempting Colormap-specific extreme-color copying.
When a user compares the resulting discrete colormap against the source customized colormap, the preserved bad/under/over colors match the source configuration.
